problems.title: Promoting the output does not recover rounded Lorentz intermediates
problems.source_location: Appendix A, PDF p.21; Appendix D.2, PDF p.23; openhype/utils/lorentz.py, get_time_comp and pairwise_dist; openhype/openhype_ae/hyperbolic_ae.py, distance call
claim: Appendices A and D.2 use Lorentz maps and distances, with a radial cap for stability. The release promotes only part of the distance calculation.
analysis: Let \(R=2^{14}\), \(x=(\sqrt{R^2+1},R,0)\), and \(y=(\sqrt{R^2+2},R,1)\), with curvature parameter \(1\). Rationalization gives \[-\langle x,y\rangle_L=(3R^2+2)/(\sqrt{(R^2+1)(R^2+2)}+R^2)\], hence distance approximately \(0.962424\). Single-precision squared norms lose the unit increments before the Lorentz subtraction, so a later double-precision output cannot restore them. The points satisfy the configured cap. A distinct finite-loss CPU case had invalid gradients, whereas the corresponding CUDA controls had finite gradients. The CPU/CUDA outcomes are historical measurements from the stated source snapshot, not new runtime executions in this pass; the original recommended dependency environment remains untested.
result: The distance path is precision-sensitive. Neither universal gradient failure nor invalidity of the published CUDA training is established.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Promote operands before the squared norms, reconstructed time coordinates and Lorentz product. Keep the backend-specific passing controls; changing only the final dtype does not address prior cancellation.
problems.impact_rationale: The evidence is input- and backend-specific numerical behavior, without demonstrated central paper damage.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
